rows.purpose: Find and invoke any available command with its current keyboard meaning.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and charter section 5 E5 require a discoverable keyboard route for every operation, so the command index becomes the shared command catalogue.
requirements: Use the command table's IDs, contexts, engine availability and gates for every invocation.
Soft disclosure may change hints but must leave all commands discoverable; final keys and wording belong to stage 2.3.

rows.purpose: Obtain the separate browser experiment and its executable web assets.
rows.reason: Charter section 4 chooses one new GUI and does not inherit the 0.4 runtime; serving the separate experiment's HTML, scripts and styles is obsolete infrastructure.
rows.notes: Proposal only; owner signature pending. This is removal of the separate 0.4 browser service and its assets, not removal of entering the solving workspace; that surviving entry is rehosted in the single 1.0 GUI.

rows.purpose: Choose the explicit keyboard context used for the next actions.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and solving-workflow.md section 4.3 retain explicit key-set switching, while charter section 5 replaces the old chooser interaction.
requirements: Show the active context and effective meanings before input; a camera, filter or moving piece must not silently change them.
Route context changes through the common command layer without changing the working orbit or puzzle.

rows.purpose: Read one authoritative snapshot of the puzzle and the solver's working context.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-CHECK need consistent state and work after every action; charter section 4 replaces the browser snapshot transport with the six-layer boundary.
requirements: Publish immutable state, workspace and protection revisions together, including the full-state hash and model identity.
Mark draft predictions separately from committed labels and never give a snapshot its own execution authority.

B-005: Capture an immutable revision-consistent snapshot under the session lock, then release the lock before encoding, publishing or waiting for a consumer; verify that a deliberately stalled large-snapshot reader cannot delay other session work.

X-02: Serve checkpoint summaries from small indexed metadata without reading full checkpoint label blobs on status, snapshot, commit, undo or redo; verify latency growth with increasing checkpoint counts.

rows.purpose: Find a saved macro by orbit and intended use.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and solving-workflow.md section 6 require a macro base organized by the solver's work, rather than the old window-opening interaction.
requirements: Search and focus the same catalogue from every entry point; selecting a result must remain explicit.
Expose exact source revision, effect evidence and applicability without manufacturing a solving macro.

rows.purpose: Compare Local and Global information captured from the same puzzle revision.
rows.reason: F-FIND, F-RELATE and F-CHECK require linked comparisons; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 6 replaces the native paired-snapshot presentation.
requirements: Pair committed geometry, Local records, workspace and protection at one revision and reject mixed-revision replies.
Bind predictions to the current review and clearly distinguish them from the committed renderer state; native transport indices belong behind the platform boundary.

B-005: Capture an immutable revision-consistent snapshot under the session lock, then release the lock before encoding, publishing or waiting for a consumer; verify that a deliberately stalled large-snapshot reader cannot delay other session work.

X-02: Serve checkpoint summaries from small indexed metadata without reading full checkpoint label blobs on status, snapshot, commit, undo or redo; verify latency growth with increasing checkpoint counts.

rows.purpose: Reach the controls for checking and explicitly executing the current operation.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE, F-CHECK and F-EXECUTE retain direct access to operation work; charter section 5 requires a new interaction for this purpose.
requirements: Focus the current operation without altering its phases, target, protection or review.
Reflect current engine availability and require the same execution gate from keys, menus and controls.

rows.purpose: Read the canonical structure, geometry and mathematical names of the complete model.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-RELATE depend on these exact model facts; charter section 2 preserves model identity and mathematics while section 4 allows rehosting their query contract.
requirements: Return model-bound canonical cell and piece IDs, all moving-orbit profiles, hosting cells, affecting caps and orientation groups without relabelling.
Keep the immutable model query separate from view preferences and prove geometric correspondence for the matching model; any identity change requires its own authorized migration.

rows.purpose: Compose, check and apply a work filter while retaining the full puzzle context.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and solving-workflow.md section 4.3 keep filtering but separate work scope from mechanics and reference display.
requirements: Validate expressions and typed identity or position members before applying the exact previewed composition.
Keep mechanical analysis, interactive work scope and noninteractive references distinct; filtering must not suppress full-operation collateral or protection conflicts.

rows.purpose: Resume a useful arrangement of the workspace and its supporting tools.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-NAVIGATE retain workspace persistence, while charter section 4 replaces detached-window storage with shell-owned preferences.
requirements: Validate and persist presentation preferences independently of puzzle commits, with generations that prevent stale overwrites.
Restore the two linked views and retained work without rolling back protection; defer a busy save explicitly rather than silently losing it.

rows.purpose: See and invoke the effective keyboard actions for the current context.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-COMPOSE keep visible key meanings; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 5 replaces the keyboard window with soft disclosure.
requirements: Show effective command, Grip and Twist meanings from the same binding resolver used by physical input.
Invoke the common command layer and keep every operation available through the palette regardless of disclosed hints.

rows.purpose: Inspect a chosen piece identity and track its current location.
rows.reason: F-FIND and solving-workflow.md sections 4 and 4.3 separate tracking a piece from assigning a target, grip or camera.
requirements: Resolve model-bound typed identities against the current revision and retain the identity as the piece moves.
Inspection must not change Current, destination, buffers, grip or camera; distinguish the identity from its present occupant record.

rows.purpose: Return to the previously chosen keyboard context.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and solving-workflow.md section 4.3 retain deliberate context switching; the old bank-return control is rehosted through the shared command layer.
requirements: Remember the exact previous context and show its effective bindings on return.
Preserve user overrides and never switch orbit, execute a turn or retarget a macro as a side effect.

rows.purpose: Inspect a fixed position and the piece occupying it now.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-CHECK need positions distinguished from identities; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 2 makes that distinction part of the encoding grammar.
requirements: Keep the canonical destination fixed while resolving its occupant and labels from the current revision.
An inspection or hover must not assign solving roles, change protection, select a grip or move the camera.

rows.purpose: Reveal additional keyboard meanings when the solver wants them.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-LEARN retain this disclosure purpose; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 5 specifies soft disclosure and an expert show-all option.
requirements: Changing disclosure must never alter bindings, command availability or mechanics.
Keep disclosure levels distinct from rewards and leave the command palette complete.

rows.purpose: Choose the current piece and its destination in a shared solving context.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and F-COMPOSE retain explicit identity and destination selection; solving-workflow.md section 4.2 requires coherent per-orbit context restoration.
requirements: Validate identity and position types and their common moving orbit before one atomic context update.
Restore drafts and choices while retaining current global protection, resolving current positions and withdrawing old review and execution authority.

rows.purpose: Temporarily reach general commands and then return to the prior keyboard context.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and charter section 5 E5 preserve efficient access to tools while replacing the old Functions-bank interaction.
requirements: Expose the changed context and restore the exact prior context on explicit return.
Respect explicit user bindings and use common command availability and gates.

rows.purpose: Make an inspected piece the current working identity.
rows.reason: F-TARGET retains this explicit assignment; solving-workflow.md section 4.3 requires inspecting and assigning to remain separate actions.
requirements: Resolve the inspected identity at the current revision and validate any retained destination.
Switch orbit and workspace atomically if necessary, retaining current protection and invalidating the prior review.

rows.purpose: Focus the Local comparison of the piece with its target.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-CHECK retain Local's purpose; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 6 requires both views to remain visible and linked.
requirements: Focus or expand Local without introducing a separate third view or hiding the required linked Global context.
Compare current and target frames with fixed anchors and one shared revision.

rows.purpose: Assign an inspected position as the destination of the current piece.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and F-COMPOSE keep deliberate destination assignment; solving-workflow.md section 4.3 separates it from inspection.
requirements: Validate the fixed position, current identity and common moving orbit before changing the role.
Retain the other roles and invalidate frame-dependent analysis, preview and execution authority.

rows.purpose: Focus the Global relationship between the piece, target and buffers.
rows.reason: F-RELATE retains Global's purpose; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 6 requires linked Global and Local views rather than the old window.
requirements: Locate the roles in the actual complete structure at the same revision as Local.
Focusing Global must not hide Local, change roles or silently remap turn keys.

rows.purpose: Choose a working orbit and recover its saved solving context.
rows.reason: F-TARGET, F-ENDGAME and solving-workflow.md section 4.2 require returning to an orbit without losing its draft.
requirements: Commit orbit and workspace changes atomically, including follow-up focus fields, so any save failure leaves both unchanged.
Resolve saved identities in current state, retain global protection and invalidate old execution permission; selecting the current orbit is a no-op.

rows.purpose: Bookmark an explicit next piece and destination.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and solving-workflow.md sections 3.3 and 4.2 give a locked Next priority while keeping it a solver choice.
requirements: Store an identity and fixed destination in the same moving orbit; replacing a bookmark must be explicit.
Keep Next independent of protection and do not activate or execute it automatically.

rows.purpose: Clear the solver's next-work bookmark.
rows.reason: F-TARGET retains deliberate control of Next under solving-workflow.md section 4.2.
requirements: Clear only the bookmark through a workspace command, retaining Current, draft, protection and journal state.

rows.purpose: Explicitly begin work on the bookmarked next piece.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and solving-workflow.md section 4.2 retain locked Next activation without choosing or executing a solving macro.
requirements: Consume the bookmark and update orbit, Current and destination in one transaction or retain all of them on failure.
Restore saved work with fresh position resolution, current global protection and no reused execution authority.

rows.purpose: Locate the bookmarked next piece without beginning its work.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-TARGET need location independently of activation; solving-workflow.md section 4.3 keeps inspection and assignment separate.
requirements: Follow the Next identity to its current position while leaving Current, roles, protection and operation authority untouched.
Report an absent or stale bookmark explicitly.

rows.purpose: Assign an inspected fixed position as buffer A.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-ENDGAME retain explicit buffer roles; solving-workflow.md section 3.1 distinguishes buffer positions from their changing occupants.
requirements: Validate the active orbit and distinct A/B positions, retain B and show A's current occupant separately.
Invalidate role-dependent review and execution authority without executing any move.

rows.purpose: Reach the available actions for the solver's next-work bookmark.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and F-NAVIGATE retain discoverable Next actions under charter section 5 E5.
requirements: Offer pin, replace, clear, locate and activate through their existing command identities and current availability.
Opening actions must not consume Next or change the puzzle.

rows.purpose: Assign an inspected fixed position as buffer B.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-ENDGAME retain explicit buffer roles; solving-workflow.md section 3.1 distinguishes buffer positions from their changing occupants.
requirements: Validate the active orbit and distinct A/B positions, retain A and show B's current occupant separately.
Invalidate role-dependent review and execution authority without executing any move.

rows.purpose: Declare what the solver's complete operation is intended to achieve.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE, F-CHECK and F-ENDGAME retain the chosen goal; solving-workflow.md section 4.1 separates progress from legal execution permission.
requirements: Evaluate the declared placement, orientation, insertion, buffer, block or orbit goal against exact complete effects.
A goal does not select or generate a macro, and an unmet goal must not prohibit an otherwise legal protected operation.

rows.purpose: Assign two distinct fixed buffer positions for the current orbit.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-ENDGAME depend on explicit A/B roles under solving-workflow.md section 3.1.
requirements: Validate both positions in the working orbit and record them atomically.
Display their current occupants separately and invalidate any review, template confirmation or execution token that depends on the old roles.

rows.purpose: Require the current piece to match its exact Home arrangement.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-ENDGAME retain exact destination requirements under solving-workflow.md sections 3.3 and 3.4.
requirements: Accept Home capture only for the matching identity, destination and active orbit.
Use exact canonical slots and orientation rather than face colours, and invalidate the previous operation review.

rows.purpose: Capture the current destination arrangement as the required target frame.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-CHECK retain explicit frame requirements under solving-workflow.md sections 3.3 and 4.
requirements: Require the declared Current identity to occupy the destination before capturing its exact labels at one revision.
Keep a captured reference distinguishable from Home and invalidate any earlier review when it changes.

rows.purpose: Express block requirements in a solver-chosen legal reference.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-PROTECT retain referenced blocks; solving-workflow.md section 3.3 permits only verified common-reference relations.
requirements: Validate the finite legal word and transport required positions and labels in chronological source-to-destination order.
Changing desired block requirements must leave captured protection at its existing locations and cannot claim rigid transport without proof.

rows.purpose: Record the exact or placement-only conditions that define a working block.
rows.reason: F-TARGET, F-COMPOSE and F-PROTECT retain Home and referenced blocks under solving-workflow.md section 3.3.
requirements: Distinguish Home, exact captured and position-only requirements; a current-state capture must verify its declared occupant.
Record identity, reference, progress condition and preservation policy separately; block membership alone does not confer completion or protection.

rows.purpose: Inspect buffer A's fixed position and current occupant.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-ENDGAME retain buffer inspection under solving-workflow.md sections 3.1 and 4.
requirements: Locate the fixed A position and resolve its occupant and frame at the current shared revision.
Inspection must not reassign A or alter the operation, grip or protection.

rows.purpose: Inspect buffer B's fixed position and current occupant.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-ENDGAME retain buffer inspection under solving-workflow.md sections 3.1 and 4.
requirements: Locate the fixed B position and resolve its occupant and frame at the current shared revision.
Inspection must not reassign B or alter the operation, grip or protection.

rows.purpose: Inspect the chosen destination and its current occupant.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-COMPOSE retain destination inspection under solving-workflow.md section 4.
requirements: Show fixed destination, current occupant and wanted identity as separate facts at one revision.
Opening inspection must not retarget the operation or change grip, protection or camera.

rows.purpose: Remove a solver-chosen requirement from the working block.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and F-COMPOSE retain editable blocks under solving-workflow.md section 3.3.
requirements: Remove only the identified member requirement and invalidate dependent goal and review results.
Do not release independently captured protection or change journal state.

rows.purpose: Capture or release explicit protection at a fixed position.
rows.reason: F-PROTECT and F-CHECK retain fine-grained protection under solving-workflow.md section 3.3 and charter section 2.
requirements: Keep exact-label and occupant-only locks distinct so releasing one mode cannot release the other; release-all must have explicit scope.
Capture committed labels or occupants, enforce identical forecast restrictions at every entry point, and invalidate previews when protection changes.
Preserve the current global protection across all saved orbit contexts; restoration must not resurrect released locks.

rows.purpose: Select a named keyboard context for the current task.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-COMPOSE retain per-orbit work sets and a general command context under solving-workflow.md section 4.3.
requirements: Switch explicitly, remember the prior context and keep orbit selection separate from bank selection.
Preserve user overrides and stable Grip/Twist meanings; all 1,200 generators and every command must remain reachable without specifying 1.0 key assignments here.

rows.purpose: Move deliberately between the available keyboard contexts.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and solving-workflow.md section 4.3 retain explicit switching, while stage 2.3 decides the new context interaction.
requirements: Expose the selected context before input and cycle without executing commands, changing the active orbit or discarding bindings.
Leave context order and physical keys to the keyboard design.

rows.purpose: Give a saved keyboard context a useful personal name.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-REUSE retain recognizable reusable work sets under solving-workflow.md section 4.3.
requirements: Persist a validated display name separately from stable context identity and bindings.
Renaming must not alter command resolution, orbit selection or mechanics.

rows.purpose: Select an explicitly identified macro from the current keyboard context.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and F-COMPOSE retain keyboard selection of fixed library entries under solving-workflow.md section 4.
requirements: Bind each shortcut to a visible exact macro ID, version and recipe, and check that binding before selection.
Selection must not insert, execute, substitute a different macro or choose one automatically from the target; insertion requires the solver's separate action.

rows.purpose: Choose which whole orbits the complete operation must preserve.
rows.reason: F-PROTECT and F-CHECK retain orbit protection under charter section 2 and solving-workflow.md section 2.
requirements: Capture current state for an unfinished protected orbit and check full labelled effects, including filtered regions.
Keep explicit unlocks authoritative, show protection independently from solved status and invalidate execution authority on changes.

rows.purpose: Bind an explicit ordered set of canonical caps to the solver's Grip context.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-COMPOSE retain editable Grip captures under solving-workflow.md section 4.3.
requirements: Validate the full cap list before atomically saving visible stable mappings, retaining order and user overrides.
Captures are ergonomic work sets and must not restrict the full set of 1,200 legal generators.

rows.purpose: Review and capture the caps that can affect an inspected piece.
rows.reason: F-FIND, F-NAVIGATE and F-COMPOSE retain contextual Grip preparation under solving-workflow.md section 4.3.
requirements: Resolve the identity's current position and show its affecting caps, distinguishing them from hosting cells.
Apply the reviewed mapping only on explicit capture; later piece movement, camera changes or filtering must not silently rebind keys.

rows.purpose: Select the explicitly bound cap for the next physical turn.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-NAVIGATE retain the Grip half of the Grip/Twist editor under solving-workflow.md section 4.3.
requirements: Show the canonical cap and ordered frame for an effective binding and enforce the chosen Hold or Latch mode.
Grip selection must be separate from inspection, target assignment and camera actions and must not execute a move.

rows.purpose: Find the commands relevant to the currently selected work object.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-COMPOSE retain contextual discovery under charter section 5 E5.
requirements: Offer shared command IDs with current engine availability and fall back to the complete palette when no work object is selected.
Opening actions must leave roles, drafts and puzzle state unchanged.

rows.purpose: Inspect and explicitly choose the ordered frame of a captured cap.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-CHECK retain unambiguous frame-bound turns under solving-workflow.md section 4.
requirements: List the twelve proper ordered cap frames and their exact meanings.
Recheck context, captured cell and previous frame before saving; reject stale edits atomically and invalidate affected analysis without silently remapping turns.

rows.purpose: Inspect committed objects and the predicted objects at each operation phase boundary.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-COMPOSE retain phase inspection; solving-workflow.md section 4.1 requires predictions and committed state to remain distinct.
requirements: Bind detached inspection to the full state, workspace, protection and selected source revisions, and reject stale results.
Show intermediate prefixes as unchecked until their protection is actually checked; inspection never grants execution permission or publishes predicted labels as committed state.

rows.purpose: Read every legal axis and inverse witness for an explicitly named cap.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-NAVIGATE depend on legal Grip/Twist mathematics; charter section 2 preserves all 1,200 generators and finite chronological witnesses.
requirements: Preserve canonical cap IDs, legal directions, signed words and inverse relationships for the full model.
Keep any retained zero-based index conversion explicit and separate from canonical identity; prove the query against the matching model rather than a visible subset.

rows.purpose: Enter explicit physical turns into a draft or execute them as guarded live turns.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-EXECUTE retain solver-entered turns; solving-workflow.md section 4.1 requires distinct draft and live paths.
requirements: Recheck the full-state hash, model and exact Grip/frame or verified input mapping before resolving the complete finite word.
Draft input changes only the selected phase; live input requires the solver's explicit action, active protection and no conflicting pending preview, and cannot borrow later cleanup.
Prevent committing input from key repeat and preserve a durable applied receipt even if its subsequent display refresh fails.

C-04: Validate draft edits and preview staging before changing phases, source receipts or recorded-scramble provenance; a rejected edit or preview must preserve the prior draft and source classification so the next journal receipt still reports the correct scramble provenance.

X-02: Serve checkpoint summaries from small indexed metadata without reading full checkpoint label blobs on status, snapshot, commit, undo or redo; verify latency growth with increasing checkpoint counts.

rows.purpose: Choose which phase receives the next explicit draft input.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE retains Prepare, Macro and Cleanup under solving-workflow.md section 4.
requirements: Make the active input phase explicit and persist it as workspace state.
Selecting a phase must not move labels, discard other phases or create execution permission.

rows.purpose: Choose explicitly between drafting future turns and making guarded live turns.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-EXECUTE require the draft/live separation in solving-workflow.md section 4.1.
requirements: Expose the destination before every turn and preserve it across resume without silently switching modes.
A live turn goes through the complete-operation protection and commit gates; a draft updates only predicted work.

rows.purpose: Compare the actual arrangement with the current complete-operation prediction.
rows.reason: F-CHECK retains before-and-after comparison; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 6 embeds operation summaries in the two linked views.
requirements: Use one shared context and revision with unmistakable actual and predicted evidence states.
Invalidate predictions after relevant edits, retain full collateral under filters and never treat a comparison as execution permission.

rows.purpose: Choose whether an explicitly selected Grip is held or latched.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-COMPOSE retain deliberate Grip release semantics under solving-workflow.md section 4.3.
requirements: Show the selected input mode and implement matching press, release and focus-loss behavior.
Changing the mode must not select another cap, alter its frame or execute a Twist.

rows.purpose: Enter and edit the explicit finite steps of an operation phase.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and F-COMPOSE retain the solver's own input under charter section 5's human-solve boundary.
requirements: Validate signed steps and aggregate recipe limits before publishing an edit; preserve chronological order and phase-local undo.
Invalidate the complete review after an accepted edit and retain exact source receipts for unaffected spans; a rejected edit must retain all prior work.

C-04: Validate draft edits and preview staging before changing phases, source receipts or recorded-scramble provenance; a rejected edit or preview must preserve the prior draft and source classification so the next journal receipt still reports the correct scramble provenance.

rows.purpose: Append or replace phase steps with an explicitly selected saved macro.
rows.reason: F-MACRO, F-COMPOSE and F-REUSE allow the solver's own macro reuse under solving-workflow.md section 4.1.
requirements: Validate the selected macro ID, version, recipe and insertion scope before changing the phase, retaining exact span receipts.
Replacement is explicit, any accepted change invalidates the complete review, and insertion never commits or automatically chooses another macro.

C-04: Validate draft edits and preview staging before changing phases, source receipts or recorded-scramble provenance; a rejected edit or preview must preserve the prior draft and source classification so the next journal receipt still reports the correct scramble provenance.

rows.purpose: Choose the geometric cell used for the Local comparison.
rows.reason: F-FIND, F-CHECK and F-NAVIGATE retain Local centering; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 6 supplies its new linked-view purpose.
requirements: Resolve explicit canonical cell, Current-based or Grip-based centering from the shared current context without changing solving roles.
Run engine lookups as cancellable jobs off the UI thread and show lookup errors with a recoverable continuation.

rows.purpose: Use the exact inverse of the solver's preparation as Cleanup.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and solving-workflow.md section 4 permit this deterministic composition of the solver's own steps under the human-solve boundary.
requirements: Reverse chronological step order and invert every signed primitive or star, including the validated default positive star sign.
Validate the aggregate operation before replacing Cleanup, invalidate its review and never commit the derived cleanup automatically.

C-04: Validate draft edits and preview staging before changing phases, source receipts or recorded-scramble provenance; a rejected edit or preview must preserve the prior draft and source classification so the next journal receipt still reports the correct scramble provenance.

rows.purpose: Check the exact complete effect of the solver's operation against its goal and protection.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and solving-workflow.md sections 2 and 4.1 require whole-operation analysis; charter section 2 preserves all labelled collateral effects.
requirements: Analyse Prepare, Macro and Cleanup together on all 259,800 labels, with finite witnesses, frame effects, collateral, residuals and every chosen protection scope.
Bind the result to state, workspace, protection and macro revisions and keep evidence, progress score and permission separate.
Report unmet goals and certificate gaps without selecting a correction macro, unlocking protection or denying an otherwise legal protected operation.

rows.purpose: Stage the exact reviewed complete operation for explicit execution.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-EXECUTE retain current-preview gating under charter section 2 and command-table.md section 1.
requirements: Recheck review revisions, full-state hash and all protected constraints before staging the exact reviewed recipe.
Replace a pending preview only explicitly; failure must restore the prior preview and execution authority without losing draft or provenance.

C-04: Validate draft edits and preview staging before changing phases, source receipts or recorded-scramble provenance; a rejected edit or preview must preserve the prior draft and source classification so the next journal receipt still reports the correct scramble provenance.

rows.purpose: Choose net-boundary or per-primitive protection for the complete operation.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-PROTECT retain Net and Strict semantics under solving-workflow.md section 2.
requirements: Net checks the end of the full chronological word; Strict checks every primitive and reports the first violation of any protected scope.
Changing the policy invalidates the review, and an unchecked prefix must never be described as safe.

rows.purpose: Explicitly execute the exact staged and currently permitted operation.
rows.reason: F-EXECUTE retains the commit contract in charter section 2 and command-table.md, with no execution without the solver's action.
requirements: Recheck preview revisions, full-state hash, model identity and all protection immediately before one atomic journal commit of the immutable witness and full collateral effects.
Commit state, work transitions and completion records consistently with a durable command ID; never repeat a committing key or classify an applied operation as failed because refresh failed.

X-02: Serve checkpoint summaries from small indexed metadata without reading full checkpoint label blobs on status, snapshot, commit, undo or redo; verify latency growth with increasing checkpoint counts.

rows.purpose: Withdraw a staged preview and its execution permission.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-COMPOSE retain explicit cancellation under command-table.md section 1.
requirements: Clear the pending preview and every corresponding execution token together.
Preserve the draft, saved macros and committed journal; a cancelled or superseded preview cannot later commit.

rows.purpose: Save an explicitly entered finite macro for later analysis and reuse.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and F-REUSE retain personal macros under charter section 5's human-solve boundary.
requirements: Validate the complete finite recipe before allocating and persisting a model-bound ID and revision with the solver's name and provenance.
Retain full collateral and exact source steps, and never generate a solving body or execute it as part of saving.

rows.purpose: Stop an analysis job and regain control of the workspace.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-PLATFORM retain cancellation under command-table.md's job and busy rules.
requirements: Keep the UI responsive and wait for cancellation acknowledgement before admitting conflicting input.
Cancelled jobs cannot publish stale analysis or execution authority, and cancelling analysis must not undo a completed commit.

rows.purpose: Inspect an explicitly selected macro's exact effect and applicability.

rows.reason: F-FIND and F-NAVIGATE retain geometric inspection under owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 6.
requirements: Keep target and current frame comparison interpretable through validated zoom ranges and shared anchors.
Zoom changes presentation only and must not relabel pieces, change pick scope or remap turns.

rows.purpose: Restore a useful default Global camera for the current geometric context.
rows.reason: F-RELATE and F-NAVIGATE retain recovery from disorienting view changes under owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 6.
requirements: Reset only Global presentation while retaining exact locations of the working piece, destination and buffers.
Keep Local linked at the same revision and preserve all solving roles, protection and bindings.

rows.purpose: Adjust the Global camera to understand relationships in the polytope.
rows.reason: F-RELATE and F-NAVIGATE retain whole-structure navigation under solving-workflow.md section 4.
requirements: Represent the actual canonical structure and keep shared role markers and the Local context consistent.
Direction commands alter the camera only; they must not turn caps, choose grips, retarget work or silently change keys.

rows.purpose: Change Global magnification to inspect structural relationships.
rows.reason: F-RELATE and F-NAVIGATE retain geometric navigation under owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 6.
requirements: Keep exact role locations and canonical adjacency interpretable through validated zoom ranges.
Magnification affects drawing only and leaves mechanics, interaction scope, Local context and turn bindings intact.

rows.purpose: Tune the geometric display for comfortable and legible work.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and charter section 5 preserve user tuning within a shared design language; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 3 requires two authored theme families.
requirements: Offer validated presentation ranges for geometric size, field of view and lighting without changing model geometry or labels.
Keep encoding, status meanings, interaction scope and protection overlays invariant across themes, and pass the full-detail renderer gate in the most expensive supported look.

rows.purpose: Control framework visibility separately from optional motion-detail presentation.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE includes two independent display purposes here: structural visibility and motion sampling; charter section 2 binds both to immutable mechanics and the full-detail renderer gate.

parts.purpose: Show or hide structural framework references for legible geometric work.
parts.reason: F-NAVIGATE retains framework visibility, and charter section 2 requires rendering choices never to change the model.
requirements: Persist a validated presentation preference without changing canonical labels, fixed structures or legal-generator reachability.
Hidden framework elements must not remove complete-effect or protection information, and pick scope must remain explicitly distinguished from noninteractive reference display.

parts.purpose: Choose optional motion-detail presentation while retaining exact full-model work.
parts.reason: F-NAVIGATE retains configurable motion presentation, while charter section 2 requires the renderer gate on all 259,800 stickers at full detail regardless of this option.
requirements: Restrict adaptive sampling to presentation; it must never alter committed labels, chronological effects, full protection analysis or canonical IDs.
Keep full detail available and restore it after motion; establish the renderer's required performance with full detail and the most complex animation, not with this option.
Make comparison, protection and picking evidence exact despite any visual sampling; this row makes no performance claim and fixes no 1.0 motion design.

rows.notes: The two coarse settings rows cover both preferences and occur in both parts; the two fine toggle rows identify separate purposes.

rows.purpose: Restore the main geometric presentation to a known useful view.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE, F-FIND and F-RELATE keep camera recovery; charter section 4 and the two-view owner decision replace the retained native camera reset.
requirements: Restore only validated camera and display defaults in the linked workspace, retaining role locations and any unsaved solving work.
Never reset puzzle labels, journal, protection, keys or the selected macro as part of a view reset.

rows.purpose: Find contextual explanations and learn the concepts used in the current work.
rows.reason: F-LEARN and F-NAVIGATE retain discoverable help under charter section 5 M1 to M6 and owner-decisions-2026-10-02-scope section 1.
requirements: Use reviewed glossary terms and real-model diagrams for the concepts actually shown, with proofs only for facts UI correctness relies on.
Keep learning optional, respect the trial text budgets with the documented error and theory exceptions, preserve work, and return focus to the owning tool.

rows.purpose: Copy an unambiguous typed mathematical name for the inspected object.
rows.reason: F-FIND, F-COMPOSE and F-REUSE retain exact names under owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 2.
requirements: Distinguish Piece identity from fixed Position and include model and naming-version evidence for reliable parsing.
Preserve exact reference and inverse notation with explicit precision; copied data must contain no private path or unrelated session information.

rows.purpose: Copy the exact canonical ID of an inspected piece or position.
rows.reason: F-FIND, F-COMPOSE and F-REUSE retain precise references under charter section 2 and owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 2.
requirements: Keep identity and fixed-position ID types explicit, preserving canonical IDs independently of camera, colour and native indices.
Copying must not assign a target or grip, alter the selected object or expose unrelated user data.

rows.purpose: Invoke one explicit command through a single responsive and guarded boundary.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM, F-COMPOSE and F-EXECUTE depend on the shared command layer defined by charter section 4 and command-table.md section 1.
requirements: Replace adapter action dispatch with stable command IDs and typed arguments using engine availability, context, busy, preview, protection and file gates as applicable.
Admit conflicting jobs atomically, keep work off the UI thread and support acknowledged cancellation without stale publication.
A durable command ID commits at most once; external callers cannot gain a route that chooses or executes a solving macro without the solver's action.

rows.purpose: Receive an authoritative command outcome with a consistently paired view result.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM, F-EXECUTE and F-CHECK require durable outcomes independent of refresh under command-table.md section 1.
requirements: Use the same command dispatch and gates for every shell path, pairing immutable view records at the resulting revision.

Preserve a durable receipt after an applied command even if snapshot or detached-inspection construction fails; report applied with display out of date and provide safe refresh instead of a failed-command retry.
Keep transport and native-index conversion behind the platform boundary.
rows.notes: The open candidate U3-006 supplies the paired snapshot used here; a read-only snapshot and an authoritative command outcome are related contracts, not interchangeable purposes.

rows.purpose: Route explicit turn input separately from inspection of clicked identities and fixed positions.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-EXECUTE can mutate draft or puzzle state, while F-FIND inspections are read-only; solving-workflow.md sections 4.1 and 4.3 require these actions to remain separate.

parts.purpose: Enter an explicit viewport turn into draft or guarded live execution.
parts.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-EXECUTE retain the explicit turn purpose under solving-workflow.md sections 4.1 and 7, rehosted through the common command layer.
requirements: Resolve the picked cap and finite signed word against the current full-state hash, model identity and verified mapping before invoking the ordinary turn command.
Draft input changes only the chosen phase and preserves prior draft and recorded-scramble provenance on rejection; live input requires fresh protection and the solver's explicit action.
Prevent repeated commit input, preserve the durable applied receipt across refresh failure and keep retained native-token translation behind the platform boundary.

X-02: Serve checkpoint summaries from small indexed metadata without reading full checkpoint label blobs on status, snapshot, commit, undo or redo; verify latency growth with increasing checkpoint counts.

parts.purpose: Inspect the current piece identity at a clicked interactive sticker.
parts.reason: F-FIND retains piece tracking under solving-workflow.md section 4.3, which separates inspection from turning and role assignment.
requirements: Resolve a visible interactive pick to the actual current occupant identity at the shared revision and verified model mapping.
Retain the identity as it moves, distinguish it from the clicked fixed position, and never turn, assign a role, release protection or select a grip as an inspection side effect.

X-02: Serve checkpoint summaries from small indexed metadata without reading full checkpoint label blobs on status, snapshot, commit, undo or redo; verify latency growth with increasing checkpoint counts.

parts.purpose: Inspect the fixed position of a clicked interactive sticker.
parts.reason: F-FIND and F-CHECK retain fixed-position inspection under solving-workflow.md section 4.3 and the encoding decision of 2 October 2026.
requirements: Resolve the pick to a canonical fixed position at the shared revision and display its changing occupant separately.
Respect interactive versus reference-only scope and verified mapping; inspection never turns, assigns a destination or grip, changes protection or grants execution authority.

X-02: Serve checkpoint summaries from small indexed metadata without reading full checkpoint label blobs on status, snapshot, commit, undo or redo; verify latency growth with increasing checkpoint counts.

rows.purpose: Export move-log evidence, inspect incoming evidence and apply confirmed evidence through separate file actions.
rows.reason: F-SESSION has distinct export, read-only inspection and transactional import purposes; AGENTS.md persistence rules and command-table.md keep their permissions and confirmation gates separate.

parts.purpose: Export the explicitly chosen verified move-log bytes.
parts.reason: F-SESSION and F-REUSE retain portable witness evidence under charter section 2 and section 5 E4.
requirements: Validate the complete model-bound history and matching import budgets before writing, with exact output byte count and digest.
Keep legacy format mapping verified and publication explicit; do not use this log as the owner-approved full-workspace migration vehicle.

parts.purpose: Inspect a move-log file and replayed endpoint before import.
parts.reason: F-SESSION retains safe read-only validation under AGENTS.md transactional input rules.
requirements: Validate complete bounded input bytes, model, format, chronological legal witnesses and replayed state without database writes.
Show affected scope and bind confirmation to the exact digest and current revisions; errors or stale input preserve all current work.

parts.purpose: Apply a freshly confirmed move-log import recoverably.
parts.reason: F-SESSION retains explicit transactional restoration under AGENTS.md persistence rules; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-migration requires the source session to remain untouched.
requirements: Recheck exact file bytes, confirmation, model, mapping and replay at the current revision before an atomic journal transition.
Retain current preferences and a recovery checkpoint or branch, invalidate stale review and execution authority, preserve the durable applied outcome and never modify the original 0.4 session.

rows.notes: The single coarse transport row covers all three actions and is repeated in each part; dedicated adapter actions U3-116, U3-117 and U3-118 implement their corresponding purposes.

rows.purpose: Refuse invocation paths that bypass the permitted command set or human-solve boundary.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM and charter section 4 require one command boundary; charter section 5 and solving-workflow.md section 7 prohibit automatic solving paths.
requirements: Reject unknown or unauthorized commands and alternate paths before state, workspace or file changes, with typed errors.
Apply the same gates to keys, controls and automation; allowed target-named setup search must remain distinct from prohibited solving-macro generation.
Keep owned shutdown and cancellation narrowly scoped without treating a transport allowlist as a filesystem or subprocess data boundary.
rows.notes: The open candidate U3-068 is not a purpose match: cancellation stops a selected job, whereas this unit refuses bypass routes.

rows.purpose: Measure bounded local backend component costs when investigating responsiveness.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM and charter section 5 E1 to E3 retain demonstrated engineering evidence, while the new runtime replaces the adapter-specific timing hook.
requirements: Make measurement opt-in, bounded and local, with declared output scope and no raw personal paths, credentials, user state or uploaded diagnostics.
Record source/build identity, tool versions and precise intervals, separating headless timings from actual Windows, input and renderer performance evidence.
Instrumentation must not influence mechanical decisions, lose committed work or run regression fixtures during normal startup.
